note: _habes pauca nomina in Sardis_ – you have only a few individuals (who have not defiled their garments). Though normally meaning “name,” _nomen_ here is the word for “person.” A similar use can be found in Rev 11:13. According to Blaise (_Dictionnaire_, p. 556), this usage is compatible with classical Latin poetry.
_nemo_ – no one else, kein anderer. In classical Latin, one would say _nemo alter_.
